STORYTIME ADVENTURES

Twenty-nine story games you play with pictures.

Sequencing, clues, feelings, retelling, memory and story paths — real comprehension adventures played right on our own storybook artwork, with plain text instructions a grown-up can read aloud.

Every card is one real game. 29 of the planned 30 adventures are playable now — 24, Unicorn's Story Choice Garden, joins the moment its artwork is uploaded. Progress is saved on this device for the child chosen in My Classroom.

FOR GROWN-UPS

What each game practises.

The collection climbs one slope: ordering stories (Bunny’s garden, Squirrel’s morning, Panda’s kite, Mouse’s train), reading picture clues (Teddy’s backpack, Rabbit’s needs, Giraffe’s detective, Otter’s hunt), matching feelings and characters (Little Lion, Owl’s world, Koala’s detective), reasoning about problems and best choices (Puppy’s helping hands, Little Bear’s decision, Squirrel’s connections), and remembering, predicting and fixing stories (Raccoon’s memory, Dragon’s endings, Penguin’s silly fixes, Turtle’s timeline, Ladybug’s missing scene, Little Deer’s paths) — up to the castle challenge that mixes them all.

Say the prompt aloud with the game, ask “why do you think so?”, and let the giggles at the silly answers do the teaching. Every worksheet twin prints without a screen.

PLAY · STORY SEQUENCING

Bunny’s Growing Garden

Bunny planted a seed, watered it, and a flower grew! Write 1, 2, and 3 in the boxes to put the pictures in story order.

Drawing on the picture needs JavaScript. Everything else on this page works without it — and the matching worksheet brings this adventure to paper.

FOR GROWN-UPS

Why this adventure helps.

This activity trains story sequencing right on the story picture: your child reads (or hears you read) one short instruction, then draws, circles and connects straight on the illustration. There is nothing to be right or wrong at — the retelling happens naturally while they draw, and saving the finished picture is the proud ending.

Prefer paper? The Bunny’s Growing Garden worksheet prints the same story with room to retell and draw — and a grown-up answer line. Printing never marks anything complete.

PLAY · PREDICTING WHAT HAPPENS NEXT

Fox’s Rainy Day Surprise

First it was sunny. Then the rain came, and Fox found a blue umbrella by the bench. What will Fox do next? Circle the picture that fits the story.

FOR GROWN-UPS

Why this adventure helps.

Prediction is the comprehension move strong readers make without noticing. Ask your child to point at the clue in the story picture before tapping — the umbrella on the bench is the whole proof.

Illustration note: The artwork tells the story twice — sunny first, rainy second — and leaves the umbrella on the bench as the clue. Answer B (beach) and C (snowman) are wonderfully silly wrong turns.

Prefer paper? The Fox’s Rainy Day Surprise worksheet prints the same story with room to retell and draw — and a grown-up answer line. Printing never marks anything complete.

This activity trains problem and solution right on the story picture: your child reads (or hears you read) one short instruction, then draws, circles and connects straight on the illustration. Prefer paper? The Squirrel’s Story Connections worksheet prints the same story with room to retell and draw — and a grown-up answer line. Printing never marks anything complete.

PLAY · STORY CHOICES

Little Deer’s Story Paths

Little Deer watches the rain. Choose the right story path — three choices lead to a rainy-day walk!

FOR GROWN-UPS

Why this adventure helps.

This is a choose-the-path game: at each fork one choice keeps the rainy-day story sensible. Ask your child to tell you WHY before tapping — the retelling is the comprehension.

Prefer paper? The Little Deer’s Story Paths worksheet prints the same story with room to retell and draw — and a grown-up answer line. Printing never marks anything complete.

Storybook Castle Challenge

Three story challenges! What happens first, how does the character feel, and what happens next?

FOR GROWN-UPS

Why this adventure helps.

A gentle finale that mixes three story skills: sequencing, feelings, and prediction. Celebrate each shield earned — three in a row unlocks the castle!
